answers.ceo-sales-01:
Hey ______, This is Chase over at Momentum. I saw that you reached out to us, and I just wanted to reach out personally and see what you were hoping we could help you with. 

What precisely is your goal? 
Why do you feel now is a definitive time to act? 
When you attempted a program in the past, what kept you from being successful? 
If we could solve/ or fix this issue, what type of impact would that have on your life? How about the peoples lives around you? 

Our first step is our Discovery Meeting. Its a 60 min complimentary session were we conduct 3 screenings. Once we have screened you, we will have the data we need to create a strategy that is specefic to you and you only. 

I have _____ and ____ available this week. Which time works best for you?
answers.ceo-sales-02: They first fall out by not responding. This is fairly common. The next place it seems they fall out is when they ask "how much does it cost" I say ““It depends on how much support you need. We have options from lower-frequency monthly training to much more comprehensive programs, but I’d rather understand what you need before recommending something you may not need.” Then the last place they fall off is if we do not sign them at the time of meeting they tend to either cancel or not respond. This is rare though
answers.ceo-sales-03: I think explaining Momentum with a sense of wonder and passion. I believe everything else is very duplicatable as is.
answers.ceo-sales-04: It does well for us in being able to intercept leads and house them in their corresponding buckets. The place where it fights me is getting my team to nurture it, the complexity in its abilities, and lastly training the AI responses to actually sound like a person and not a bot.
answers.ceo-price-01: The current pricing was a slow evolution of our services. If we rewind a few years back when I was personally training people still as my primary source of income, I was charging nearly twice as much as the other trainers and also had almost double the number of clients they had. I said why don't you guys try doing it the way I do, hence- all the add ons, communications, plans, and education. And it worked...... Some members had pushback, but other members just needed to be shown the value and they didn't bat an eye.
answers.ceo-price-02: There should only be about 10% of the population that has them. It's mostly trainers who are scared of losing their people who won't go up on them. I would absolutely be all in for cleaning them up. People shouldn't have special rates unless brought in on a scholarship, a member of our board, or an investor.
answers.ceo-price-03: Sessions get counted by checking the trainers appointments out through Mindbody, we reconcile the accounts by comparing the staff/appoinments section with our services tab. I try to keep an eye on it every single day. I run a day by day reconciliation between MINDBODY and our Worthington account. It takes me roughly 30 mins per day. Tiffany also helps double check my work.
answers.ceo-price-04: The original split which I inherited from an old business partner who ran and sold a successful gym from her. The split was 65% trainer / 35% gym. After years of trying to make this split work, after many months spent working with a business/ financial consultant we came to realize that the unit economics just didn't fit. So we took the split down to %55. I was worried at first, but with proper explanation there wasn't any pushback. My financial consultant still thinks that 45% is still to low. He recommended the best economics would be 55% gym, 45% trainer. If we dropped to that model we would surely lose trainers, unless we were able to mark the price up high enough that the pay actually increased in their favor.

answers.ceo-ops-02:
I would like too see: 
How many new members did we gain last week? 
CAC- customer acquisition cost 
CLV- customer lifetime value 
ARR- Annual recurring revenue 
MRR- Monthly recurring revenue 
ROI- return on investment with marketing and advertising 
Burn Multiple- How much cash were burning to generate each dollar of new recurring revenue. 
EBITDA- earnings before interest taxes depreciation and amortization. 
CHURN- percentage of customers who cancel 
LTV:CAC- How much value we generate for every 1$ dollar spent to acquire a customer 
NRR- Net revenue retention. The percentage of revenue retained from existing customers
Gross Margin- Our profit after direct costs and service delivery 
Operating Margin- Percentage of revenue left after all operating expenses 
CAC payback- The amount of time it takes to recover the cost of acquiring a customer from the gross profit generated by that customer. 
Cash runway- The number of months our company can operate before running out of cash, based on our current cash burn rate.
answers.ceo-ops-03: This time needs to be filled with corporate wellness programs. We just are demographically/space disadvantaged right now to pull this off yet.

answers.jo-hats-01:
I am training in the early morning, then afternoons are reserved for admin/socials & my own gym time. When all of my clients are in town, usually ~80% of the time, I'm in back to back sessions from 5am-11am every day. Depending on the week I may have an hour break somewhere in there, but not normally. 

I have been prioritizing admin work over socials for the past two months, but would like to swap that.
answers.jo-hats-02: I don't mind the actual training necessarily, but the schedule is draining. I'd love to be here 7am-3pm or somewhere in that time frame. The disorganization of the admin work can be stressful sometimes when I'm spending a lot of time trying to bring order to it, but things keep changing or procedures not followed.
answers.jo-tr-01: I use Typeset for training programs & nutrition protocols. Those are created from scratch. I use Superset for online clients & like that everything is in one place (programs, files, check ins, etc.). answers.jo-tr-03: I am not a fan of multiple Physics coaches at all. I think 1-2 people should hold that role completely, & be responsible for everything that comes with it. That way everything stays consistent & nothing gets lost in communication or execution. It's so inconsistent right now with 5 coaches, & that's my least favorite thing about it. I also dislike how the programming is sent out the night before. It needs to be done & distributed 4 weeks in advance like any regular training block. Overall, it's a great model. But I think it's being ruined by poor coach quality, a lack of effective exercise instruction, & disorganization.
answers.jo-tr-04: I am for sure bringing one. Two are a definite no (one is moving to Houston), & 3 will be on the fence. Realistically, I think two will move with us & we'll lose the rest.

answers.jo-tr-02: More information on their actual strength level. answers.jo-big-01: Organization & consistency. Everything is constantly changing & members don't like that. Trainers really don't either.
